transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-01
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 48m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Owen Li (Redwood CSM); Maya Chen (Aurelia CTO), Dan Rodrigez (Aurelia SRE), Lee Taylor (Aurelia PM), Sofia Patel (Aurelia Security)

Summary:
Quick closure and commitment call after last week's outage (aftershock event). Focus: root cause confirmation, mitigations implemented, telemetry gaps, security/compliance asks, and next steps to close the escalation.

Topics Covered:
- RCA review (KV cache eviction pattern + autoscaler interaction)
- Recent mitigations (circuit-breaker, canary rollback policy, prewarm pools)
- Telemetry and trace gaps (span sampling, token-level latency buckets)
- Security/audit requests (SOC2 docs, KMS/HSM questions, SSO assertion logs)
- Pilot plan and benchmarks for Dedicated capacity

Action items (brief): see metadata list above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): all right folks, thanks for joining, uh we'll try to keep this tight. um main purpose is to close the follow-up from last week's aftershock and confirm commitments. maya, dan — how are you all holding?
[00:09] Maya (Aurelia CTO): yeah thanks Alex, uh we've got teams on standby. there's still some nervousness around the KV cache behavior and the autoscaler interaction — that's our top ask.
[00:18] Dan (Aurelia SRE): yeh the thing that bit us was a duplicate eviction wave, it sort of cascaded with the horizontal pod autoscaler and then the canary didn't fail open like we expected. the prefix caching wasn't being restored quickly enough.
[00:28] Priya (Redwood SE): okay, quick note — in our initial root cause we saw an edge case where under certain request bursts the continuous-batcher would flush cached KV pointers, the kv key references were rehydrated but on a slower path. that plus aggressive pod spin up caused token timing spikes.
[00:43] Lee (Aurelia PM): is the problem specifically the KV cache corruption or the timing between cache miss and new pod readiness?
[00:51] Priya (Redwood SE): mostly the latter. the cache entries were fine in storage, but the warm path — the K V cache warm path — was on a cold startup CPU-optimized code-path instead of the quantized fast path, so latency spiked and the autoscaler saw latency and then scaled.
[01:10] Dan (Aurelia SRE): that lines up with our traces; you can see tail latency climb, then multiple pods start, then we get a thundering retry pattern.
[01:18] Alex (Redwood AE): and that triggered your fallback rules in the app which amplified retries?
[01:22] Dan (Aurelia SRE): correct. we had retry glue in the gateway. so a few things aligned badly.
[01:29] Maya (Aurelia CTO): for us the split is: we need a fix that reduces blast radius, and we need observability to show the chain.
[01:37] Priya (Redwood SE): implemented mitigations since last call: 1) introduced a short-lived prewarm pool for hot-model shards to remove the cold path, 2) adjusted autoscaler thresholds to be more conservative around token-latency, 3) added a circuit-breaker so requests see a graceful fallback to a smaller model instead of retrying.
[01:55] Sofia (Security): quick security interjection — will any of these changes change our data residency or add new logging that could conflict with our retention policy?
[02:03] Priya (Redwood SE): no changes to residency, but we will increase some debug logging temporarily for the bench. we can mask PII and make logs ephemeral.
[02:12] Lee (Aurelia PM): can you restate the rollback and canary policy? cause last time the canary didn't fall back fast enough.
[02:19] Alex (Redwood AE): yep. we built an automatic fallback that monitors median and 95th percentile token latency per route. if both cross thresholds for two consecutive 30s windows, we auto-roll to the previous model and notify. the failure mode we saw was the decision window being too long and the canary not having enough traffic.
[02:38] Maya (Aurelia CTO): so to be clear, you'll shorten the decision window and force a manual guardrail?
[02:43] Owen (Redwood CSM): we can shorten the decision window to 20s and add a manual 'panic button' in the console that Aurelia ops can press to immediately route off the canary.
[02:53] Dan (Aurelia SRE): that would help, the other thing is the token accounting — we need better token-level latency buckets exposed. right now we have coarse metrics.
[03:03] Priya (Redwood SE): agreed. we'll enable token-bucket histograms and add a tracing tag that surfaces the cache-warm vs cold start path. there is a small perf cost but it's worth it for triage.
[03:16] Maya (Aurelia CTO): on the compliance front: we're still waiting for the SOC2 point-in-time attestation and KMS integration details. that will determine if we can move to Dedicated.
[03:25] Alex (Redwood AE): action: I'll send the SOC2 pack and KMS/HSM integration doc after this call. also we'll include SSO assertion samples for your security team.
[03:33] Sofia (Security Lead): also want to see audit logs at token granularity for 30 days, is that doable?
[03:39] Priya (Redwood SE): currently token-level audit for 30d is an add-on; we can enable a retention window and ship the logs to your S3/MSS solution with encryption via customer KMS.
[03:52] Dan (Aurelia SRE): quick note — we reproduced the repro in staging but it's been flaky; we'll upload the pod logs and the KV trace, you'll need them for the bench.
[04:00] Alex (Redwood AE): awesome, please upload. Priya — can you run the micro-bench against our NVidia A100 profile early next week? the idea is to measure warm vs cold path latencies and show expected P95/P99 under load.
[04:12] Priya (Redwood SE): yes, I'll provision a dedicated test pool and run 3 runs at 1k rps, 5k rps, and 10k rps. we'll capture token spans, batching behavior, and startup tail.
[04:24] Lee (Aurelia PM): what about Dedicated? if we go dedicated, do we still see this old path?
[04:30] Priya (Redwood SE): Dedicated helps because you can pin GPUs and keep warmed pools. it reduces cold-start probability significantly. however incorrect autoscaler interaction can still cause a degraded warm path on bursty traffic if the prewarm pool is mis-sized.
[04:44] Maya (Aurelia CTO): pricing question will be decisive for us. if Dedicated plus the audit add-on fits our cost model we'll proceed to pilot.
[04:52] Alex (Redwood AE): we'll provide a pilot quote — committed throughput and a bounded overage plan. we'll include the audit/logging add-on as a separate line.
[04:59] Dan (Aurelia SRE): regarding the telemetry gap — we noticed some spans were dropped during the incident; is that instrumentation or exporter throttling?
[05:05] Priya (Redwood SE): a bit of both. exporter backpressure plus a sampling rule that threw away low-level KV traces once the buffer hit 80%. we've adjusted sampling to preserve cache-warm markers and will ship a patch to the exporter.
[05:20] Maya (Aurelia CTO): great. timeline to close the ticket?
[05:23] Alex (Redwood AE): propose we close the escalation if: 1) logs and KV traces are shared, 2) bench results show P95 improvement and lower tail on warmed pool, 3) security pack received, 4) pilot quote accepted or next meeting scheduled. target close: next Friday (Dec 10).
[05:40] Sofia (Security Lead): we also need to confirm that longterm retention doesn't expose customer PII; we'll send a sample list of required audit fields.
[05:48] Owen (Redwood CSM): noted — we'll make sure the logging pipeline masks PII before persistence.
[05:52] Lee (Aurelia PM): quick question about fallback accuracy — you mentioned smaller model fallback, does that mean quality regressions?
[05:59] Priya (Redwood SE): yes slight quality delta. fallback is tuned to be conservative — it's used to preserve latency SLOs for interactive paths. for batch pipelines we recommend queueing rather than fallback.
[06:10] Dan (Aurelia SRE): for our internal runbooks we need an explicit playbook entry: if token latency > X and cache warm fraction < Y then trigger reroute. can you produce that?
[06:19] Alex (Redwood AE): yes, Priya and I will draft a runbook snippet and put it in the shared binder.
[06:24] Priya (Redwood SE): plus I'll add a tracing dashboard and a pre-populated query for warm-vs-cold path.
[06:31] Maya (Aurelia CTO): ok, sounds good. any other risks we should know about?
[06:35] Priya (Redwood SE): there's a residual risk around long tail when model size grows; quantization and kernel selection help but we recommend active monitoring and periodic benching.
[06:46] Dan (Aurelia SRE): also to call out the gateway retry policy, we recommended moving to idempotent-safe retries and bounded retry budgets at the gateway.
[06:55] Alex (Redwood AE): agreed, we'll share a recommended gateway config.
[07:00] Lee (Aurelia PM): how will we know when to switch from Hosted to Dedicated? what are the triggers?
[07:06] Owen (Redwood CSM): triggers we've seen are: steady-state throughput > X tokens/sec for 7 days, SLA risk events, and security requirement like KMS-only or air-gap. we can make the threshold explicit in the pilot quote.
[07:18] Maya (Aurelia CTO): good. let's lock down the bench and the SOC2 paperwork.
[07:23] Alex (Redwood AE): action recap: I'll send security docs and pilot draft; Priya will run benchmarks and produce dashboards; Dan will upload logs; Sofia will provide compliance fields. target internal close by 2026-12-10.
[07:36] Maya (Aurelia CTO): thanks everyone. appreciate the quick turnaround.
[07:40] Alex (Redwood AE): thanks all — we'll follow up in email with the timeline.
[07:44] call ends
